questions.question: When getting ready to change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors to see traffic behind you. Just before you move into the new lane, glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with a headlight and reflector. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to avoid dangerous collisions.

questions.question: This sign indicates that:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not pay attention to how many tracks there are to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains or other vehicles. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you want to change lanes or move your vehicle left or right, signal first to alert other drivers. Always check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road than on a dry road. Keep a longer distance between you and the car ahead when driving on slippery roads.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: If you see animals standing near the roadway while driving:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. There may also be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a crossroad ahead.

questions.question: What should you do to cross a railroad safely?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look both ways for trains from either direction before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By staring straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure loose items before moving your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Should a driver yield the right-of-way to a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with disabilities using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device have the right-of-way. They have the same rights as other pedestrians on sidewalks or roadways.

questions.question: Which statement is true about railroad crossings?

options.text: Use cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
You must stop when a flagger or stop sign tells you to at a railroad crossing.
You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop when a flagger or stop sign tells you to at a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal directs you to stop. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Change lanes only when needed. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be prepared to stop to avoid hitting the pedestrian.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what other cars are doing instead of following the flagger.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow regular traffic laws and ignore the construction zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Follow all directions from flaggers in construction zones. Slow down and obey signs and flagger instructions. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Don't drink if you are going to drive.
The road is slippery when wet.
The road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does excessive speed do?

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of car crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving if you take any medicine. Tell them especially if you take tranquilizers or sedatives.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: To prevent tired driving, take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving duties with another person so you can each rest while the other drives.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as far. Low visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let others pass if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangle sign means you must yield. Slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Stop heavy bleeding by pressing on the wound. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Build a habit when you get in your car. Before you start the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: You must let a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog cross:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without red tips) always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both drugs may have stronger effects.
Nothing will happen.
Both drugs may have weaker effects.
Only the alcohol may have weaker effects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both drugs may have stronger effects.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A railroad worker signals you to stop.
A stop sign is posted there.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down and working.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a railroad worker signals you to stop or when a stop sign is there. Stop when red lights are flashing and gates are down and working.

questions.question: A driver taking an over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Read the label before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Keep driving no matter what the label says.
Only drive during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label before driving.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. If you take any medicine, even cold or allergy remedies, check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking it.
